title: Trombone method books and how he began
summary: Method books he used, solfege questions, and a teacher saying he was a natural.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Are there any good books on trombone? Do you remember the book you started with? Yeah.
Yeah, I used to, Ben Verricon. That was one of the first books I got, Ben Verricon.
Ben Verricon, yeah. I think they still got those books, yeah.
Ben Verricon. Published by Carl Fisher. Yeah, yeah, that's right. When you started on trombone, you remember the book that your uncle gave you or anything?
Yeah, I can't think of the name. Now, let's see. His name is a book now. I'll give this boy one. He's good. A trumpet? Yeah. I can't think of that mouthpiece. That book.
That's it. I think that's it.
Yeah, they got everything now. Arbonne. That's the book I gave him. Oh, he's nice. You should hear him play.

Well, when you started, did you, I know Bunk tells about when he started on trumpet. He studied at school and had a Mexican teacher and made him study solfetch. Yes, yes. The sight reading. Yes, sight reading. Did you have to go through that before you took up your instrument? Or how did you think?

Well, it seemed like to me that, I don't know, the man said that it was natural for me. See? Because I have a large lip and I played in a large mouthpiece. And he said it was natural for me that I didn't have the words. And he told me, he said, you're going to come to be one of the best trombone players of tears. I didn't think he'd do it. I just played just to, you know. Yeah, he could tell. Make a little air. He could tell, you know, from the way I handled the instrument. He said, you'll be one of the best of tears. But I didn't play that no more. I tell fellas, not. He's another fella, too. There's a fella by the name of Zoo Robertson. I didn't talk about him.
